summary: Round-1's AmCache DACL-verifier fix authored D:P(A;OICI;GA;;;OW) as the scratch directory's SDDL and then verified the resulting ACE's SID against {owner_sid, WinLocalSystemSid, WinBuiltinAdministratorsSid}. OW (SDDL_OWNER_RIGHTS, S-1-3-4) is stored VERBATIM in a DACL and never substituted to a concrete SID -- only CO (CREATOR_OWNER, S-1-3-0) undergoes SID substitution, and only during inheritance to a NEW child object. The verifier could therefore never match on any real host. Independently confirmed via icacls on a freshly created scratch directory on the-rig: SDDL D:P(A;OICI;FA;;;OW), owner BUILTIN\Administrators -- the ACE's SID is literally S-1-3-4, not the owner's SID. AmCache was permanently constrained|dest_dir_acl on every real install; round-1's own the-rig test evidence ('32 test cases passed') was a false-green, since the test's has_success_row || has_constrained_row assertion accepts either outcome.
trigger: unconditional on every real Windows install -- no attacker or special condition needed, the verifier's SID comparison is structurally unsatisfiable
disposition_note: Redesigned entirely rather than patched: collect_amcache now uses yuzu_create_temp_dir (agents/core/src/temp_file.cpp -- 128-bit BCryptGenRandom name, CREATE_NEW semantics) for a per-dispatch random scratch directory under agent.data_dir, with a new ScratchDirGuard RAII wrapper for removal and scratch_dir_is_ours(HANDLE) verifying ownership via EqualSid against the CURRENT PROCESS TOKEN's owner (GetTokenInformation(TokenOwner)) rather than a hardcoded SID list or a DACL walk. This eliminates the SDDL-authoring/OW-verification mismatch structurally -- there is no longer any SDDL string to author or ACE to compare against. New win-local test (test_execution_artifacts_win_local.cpp) explicitly asserts a permanently-broken leg reddens independently of the success/constrained OR, closing the false-green class. Not yet independently rebuilt/re-verified on real Windows in this round -- flagged as the single largest open verification risk in the remediation plan; the-rig build+test pass is still pending.

line: parse_prefetch volume-walk block (~572-606 at review time)
summary: The Prefetch parser's volume-walk only read and validated the FIRST volume entry in the file-information block; on a real multi-volume .pf file, entries 1+ were never bounds- or consistency-checked. Separately (self-found during verification, not flagged by the reviewer): file_ref_count was being set to the refs sub-block's VERSION DWORD (constant 3) rather than the true per-entry file-reference COUNT -- a wrong-result bug on every single-volume file too, not just multi-volume ones. Byte-verified against 3 real .pf.decompressed fixtures: true per-file totals are DOSKEY 15 (1 volume), OUTPUT 23 (2 volumes, 7+16), REG.EXE 32 (2 volumes, 3+29) -- the parser reported 3 for all three before this fix.
trigger: any real Prefetch file with more than one volume entry (entries 1+ unvalidated); file_ref_count is wrong on EVERY Prefetch file, single- or multi-volume
disposition_note: Rewrote the volume-walk into a full per-entry loop with bounds+consistency checks: 96-byte stride for v30/31 (pinned against real two-volume fixtures -- entry 1 decodes to a valid \VOLUME{...} path at offset 96, garbage at 104), 104-byte stride for v23/26 (libscca-documented, unpinned by any real capture in this repo -- the existing bounds/consistency checks fail closed on a wrong stride, so an incorrect documentation-derived value cannot silently succeed). file_ref_count is now the sum of each entry's true count (read from the refs sub-block's count field, validated against its declared byte size), capped at the existing kPrefetchMaxFileRefs invariant. Real-fixture assertions updated to the byte-derived totals (15/23/32). Mutation-tested: reverted the loop bound to simulate the old single-entry bug, confirmed exactly the expected test cases/assertions reddened, restored, re-verified green (30/30 cases, 65244 assertions on macOS).

disposition_note: scratch_dir_is_ours(HANDLE) now compares against the CURRENT PROCESS TOKEN's owner (OpenProcessToken + GetTokenInformation(TokenOwner)), not a hardcoded SID list -- works correctly under any identity the agent process happens to run as, including a future NT SERVICE\YuzuAgent account. Narrows (does not close) #4450: the AmCache leg specifically is now least-privilege-ready, but ShimCache and Prefetch's own unmeasured-privilege status is unaffected by this round's changes.

summary: MANDATORY INVESTIGATION resolved live on the-rig (2026-09-17), first real MSVC compile+run of the round-2 AmCache redesign: root-caused directly rather than guessed at. Copied C:\Windows\appcompat\Programs\Amcache.hve, `reg load`ed it into a scratch hive key, and `reg query`d the specific subkeys the win-local test's elevated run produced empty-field rows for. Confirmed: several InventoryApplicationFile subkeys (built-in driver files -- 1394kdbg.sys, 1394ohci.sys -- confirmed by name) genuinely carry ONLY ProgramId and FileId in the registry itself, no LowerCaseLongPath/Size/LinkDate/Publisher/BinaryType/ProductName/ProductVersion values at all. Real AmCache data sparseness on this Windows 11 26200 build, not a value-read defect -- get_or_empty() (execution_artifacts_parsers.hpp) correctly returns "" for a value genuinely absent from that subkey. ~73% of the 10001 real amcache rows in the fresh capture show this shape, confirming it is a widespread, not rare, characteristic.
